svg.aria-label: A component diagram of the mastering chain: each theme's voices land on a mono kick and bass bus and on drums, keys and melodic buses with their rooms, are ducked, widened and filtered, and leave through the theme's own loudness trim; the set's shared tail is a DC block, the master EQ, the make-up gain, a look-ahead limiter, a soft clipper and the output route to the audio device; a timing panel shows one kick ducking the melodic bus and the bass, and the limiter's look-ahead.

g.text: kick · sub · hats · shaker · clap · keys · pad · piano · effects — synthesised, never sampled
peak dB under the master bus: kick −3.0 · sub −14.0 · clap −5.5 · hats −5.5 and −5.0
each voice lands on one bus, and feeds the rooms beside it by its own send amount
mono by construction, not by rule
+1.5 dB of sub at a drop
kick and bass, one mono bus
nothing at all through a groove
a compressor here clicks in Firefox
no duck: straight to the macro filter
the keys, through a slow chorus
wet 0.42 each, into the melodic bus
and the keys bus above it
one ramp per kick — the rooms duck too
mid/side: the mid is never touched
lowpass, 420 Hz closed to 15 kHz open
below the corner there is no side
built the first time a piano sends
the theme’s dice and its events
read once, before a note sounds
fitted at plan time, one per theme
from the theme’s dice and its plan
so no theme arrives louder than another
and a fader of its own
two decks at a seam, one master
keeps the sub off the bell
no worklet: the set runs 2 dB lower
silent — the checks, a gain of zero
unity again at 0.95 of the beat
gain, as far as the peak asks
look-ahead 5 ms: the gain moves first, and the audio is held the same 5 ms
release 200 ms — the ceiling is 0.75, and the clipper behind it cannot pass 0.891
ms, the kick at zero — a beat is 582 ms at 103 BPM
